blockers: The card or coin is not reliably legible at native 1x; the signature prop collapses into a tiny hand highlight or isolated pixel cluster.

The silhouette is dominated by two parallel green lower-body columns. Coat tails, legs, knees, and ankles merge, replacing the intended broken-diagonal gambler shape with a symmetrical mannequin profile.

The locomotion grid shows pose changes but not convincing weight transfer. The long coat obscures the support leg, and the feet lack readable heel-to-toe action, making several directions read as sliding rather than stepping.
The idle strip is an almost rigid front-facing hold with insufficient torso, shoulder, hip, or coat movement to establish a jaunty theatrical rhythm.
The facial structure collapses into a pale horizontal mask beneath a heavy brim. Eye line, nose, mouth, and jaw do not form a readable expression at 1x and produce a mannequin-like neutral face.
There is no convincing secondary-motion hierarchy. The duster, fedora ribbon or feather, and prop do not visibly lag, overshoot, or settle behind the primary action.
Material separation is inadequate in the lower body: dark trousers and coat shadows merge, while the red vest reads as a flat color block rather than distinct velvet against the duster.
high_value_changes: Redesign the lower silhouette first: separate the coat tails from the legs, expose a readable knee and ankle gap, taper the tails asymmetrically, and establish one clearly weight-bearing leg in the key poses.

Rebuild each 8-frame walk cycle from explicit contact, passing, push-off, airborne, and recovery poses. Add hip and shoulder counter-rotation, a visible planted foot, and directional stride asymmetry rather than simply moving the legs under a fixed coat.

Re-author the signature flourish with clear anticipation, a broad readable card or coin arc, a held reveal, wrist overshoot, and a settle. The prop must remain a distinct high-contrast shape at native 1x.

Simplify and enlarge the facial planes: preserve a visible eye band beneath the brim, define a graphic nose and jaw break, and give the mouth a deliberate gambler expression instead of a generic horizontal facial stripe.
Add delayed secondary motion to the duster tails, ribbon or feather, and prop, with at least a one- to two-frame lag and visible settle after the hand stops.

Rebalance values so the trousers, coat shadows, and inner leg gap do not collapse into one dark mass. Use a controlled highlight plane to distinguish emerald fabric from red velvet without relying on smooth plastic-looking gradients.
optional_notes: The measured 119.3px height and 0.0px anchor drift satisfy the hard size and positioning constraints, but they do not validate visual foot contact or animation quality.
The emerald, crimson, and violet hue grouping is more useful than the internal material modeling; the fedora accent is currently the only dependable diagonal silhouette cue.
The full 8-direction frame coverage is present, but coverage is not equivalent to readable or directionally consistent locomotion.
regressions_from_previous: No round-01 visual sheets or metric comparison were supplied, so regressions cannot be verified. The unresolved readability and motion failures must be treated as carryover risk until a side-by-side comparison is provided.
strongest_improvements: Hard technical compliance is intact: the standing sprite remains below the 128px ceiling and the ground anchor is stable.
The basic emerald duster and crimson vest color coding survives both dark and light inspection backgrounds.
The tilted fedora and small green diagonal accent provide a partial identity cue, though they are insufficient without a readable prop and stronger pose.
luna_evaluation.single_most_important_next_change: Redesign the native-1x key silhouette around one visibly planted asymmetric leg, separated coat tails, and a 3-5px high-contrast card or coin flourish; then propagate that readable weight-and-prop relationship through the walk and gesture cycles.
